name: SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program)
description: Monthly food assistance on a Lone Star EBT card. IMPORTANT for Texas: under Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE), most Texas households are screened against a 165% FPL gross-income limit, not the federal 130% baseline. Households with an elderly (60+) or disabled member must instead pass a 100% FPL net-income test. Qualified noncitizens may be eligible; many children qualify regardless of their parents' status.
documents_needed: Social Security numbers for all household members
Proof of income (last 30 days of pay stubs)
Proof of address (utility bill or lease)
source: Texas HHSC Texas Works Handbook C-121 (rev. Oct 2025); USDA FNS

name: WIC (Women, Infants, and Children)
description: Food benefits, nutrition education, and breastfeeding support. CATEGORICAL requirement the schema can't express: the household must include a pregnant woman, a postpartum/breastfeeding woman (up to 1 year), an infant, or a child under age 5. Income limit is 185% FPL, and households on SNAP, Medicaid, or TANF are adjunctively income-eligible automatically. No citizenship requirement.
source: Texas WIC Policy CS:12.0; USDA WIC 2025/26 income guidelines (90 FR, eff. July 1, 2025)

name: Free & Reduced-Price School Meals (NSLP/SBP)
description: Free or reduced-price breakfast and lunch at school. Free meals at or below 130% FPL; reduced-price at or below 185% FPL. Children in SNAP/TANF households are directly certified — no application needed. Requires a child enrolled in a participating school.
documents_needed: School meal application via the child's school district
source: USDA FNS income eligibility guidelines 2025-26 (eff. July 1, 2025)

name: Lifeline Phone & Internet Benefit
description: Up to $9.25/month off phone or internet service ($34.25 on Tribal lands). Income at or below 135% FPL, or automatic eligibility through SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, WIC, or other qualifying programs.
documents_needed: Proof of income or program participation (SNAP/Medicaid/SSI award letter)

name: Medicare Savings Programs (QMB/SLMB/QI)
description: Pays Medicare Part B premiums (and sometimes deductibles/copays) for Medicare enrollees with limited income: QMB ~100% FPL, SLMB ~120%, QI ~135%. Requires being on Medicare — typically age 65+ or disability + 24 months of SSDI. Texas resource limits also apply.

name: Medicare Extra Help (Part D Low-Income Subsidy)
description: Covers most Medicare Part D prescription drug costs — worth about $5,300/year. Income limit ~150% FPL with resource limits. Must be enrolled in Medicare. Automatic for people who also get Medicaid, SSI, or a Medicare Savings Program.

name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
description: Monthly cash benefit (~$967/mo individual, $1,450/mo couple in 2026) for people who are 65+, blind, or disabled with very limited income and resources. Requires age 65+ OR a qualifying disability — the schema can't express OR, so screen on the disability flag. In Texas, SSI recipients are automatically enrolled in Medicaid.
documents_needed: Proof of age and citizenship/immigration status

name: Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)
description: Monthly benefit for workers who become disabled and have sufficient work credits. Not income-tested — based on work history and a qualifying disability. Beneficiaries get Medicare after a 24-month waiting period.

name: ACA Marketplace Premium Tax Credits
description: Subsidized health insurance through HealthCare.gov (Texas uses the federal marketplace). Requires household income of at least 100% FPL — the schema only stores a ceiling, so the matcher must also apply the floor. CRITICAL TEXAS NOTE: adults under 100% FPL fall in the coverage gap (Texas did not expand Medicaid) — flag this instead of matching. Must be lawfully present and not eligible for Medicaid/CHIP or affordable employer coverage.
documents_needed: Income estimate for the coverage year
Social Security numbers or immigration documents
source: HealthCare.gov; IRS premium tax credit rules (26 U.S.C. 36B)
